items.title: Ignacio Berroa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 22, 2021 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: Mario became my mentor, it was Mario the guy that took me to the union musicians in New York.

ctx.x: And here you are, you’re in the country for about a year and can you tell me how all of a sudden you appear in a club as Dizzy Gillespie’s drummer?

Life is full of surprises. I arrived to New York and I got in touch with the Cuban musician Mario Bauza who was responsible for that Afro-Cuban jazz movement in the 40s it was Mario who told Dizzy to hire Chano Pozo and so forth and so on and the rest is history. So I met Mario. Mario became my mentor, it was Mario the guy that took me to the union musicians in New York. He recommended me with different musicians in New York, mainly those who went into the recording industry like Arturo Chico O’Farrill to name…

imagine all the drummers that Dizzy had on his phone book. So after calling everybody or I don’t know, whatever, and it turns out that everybody was busy, he remembered, oh Mario told me about a Cuban drummer. So he called Mario and Mario told him, “Let me see if the guy is available.” I was available and that’s how I ended up playing this night, six months after my arrival to the United States I was sitting behind Dizzy Gillespie on drums playing at a club in Manhattan called Fat Tuesday. items.title: Ignacio Berroa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 24, 2021 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: by that time Mario and I were friends, we were friends

ctx.x: No. No, no, no, no, no, no. He was, one day he had an engagement in New York. He was desperate looking for his drummer because his favorite drummer wasn’t able to leave Boston because they shut down the city due to a snowstorm and Dizzy had an engagement at a club in New York at Fat Tuesday. So Dizzy, once his drummer told him that he wasn’t able to arrive to New York, he has been looking for drummers. He opened up his phone book and started calling people, calling people, calling people. Everybody was busy and…

“Do you think that that guy you told me is available?” And Mario told him, “Okay, let me call him up, I don’t know if he is available.” Mario called me, I was available, and then Mario said to me, okay — it was very funny because the phone rang and Mario asked me, “Do you want to play with Dizzy Gillespie tonight?” Out of the clear blue that was the question and by that time Mario and I were friends, we were friends, and I told him, “Mario come on, you’re too old for this type of joke at this time.” And then he…
